_what: Inputs to the campaign rate budget Theoria.md:299 asks for. Declared here rather than recomputed from the ledger on every run, so the budget is deterministic and a change to it is a diff somebody has to justify. `rate_budget.py --measure` recomputes the measured inputs from the tracked data files and reports drift against these declarations; verify.sh runs it.

limit.source: docs.arcprize.org/rate_limits.md, quoted in ACCESS_CHECK.md §6 and browser-ops/TERMS.md:31
limit.breach: HTTP 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, then progressively longer backoff
limit._observed_breaches: Zero 429s in 3,736 logged requests across arc-recon/data/recon_ledger.jsonl (1231), baseline-arms/ledger.jsonl (560) and baseline-arms/probe_log.jsonl (1945), audited 2026-07-28 under S5. The gate has never been seen to close. Everything below is therefore a bound derived from the documented number, not a calibration against observed behaviour -- see ACCESS_CHECK.md §6d's residual.

measured._rtt: min and median of elapsed_ms over 1231 requests in data/recon_ledger.jsonl (2026-07-28). rtt_min is the one that matters: it is the fastest a single process can possibly issue back-to-back requests, so it sets the worst-case rate.
measured._attempts: post: 20 commands / 20 HTTP and 16/16 on the two cookie-jar sweeps in data/canary_runs.jsonl (INC-007a). pre: 190 HTTP / 20 commands on the paired cookie-less sweep.

worker_shapes.what: An arm that calls a model between actions. The model call, not the API, sets the pace.
worker_shapes._think_s: Deliberately optimistic. baseline-arms measured wall clocks implying far longer per action (S1: 4,227 attempted actions in 45.8 h on haiku). A smaller think time makes the rate WORSE, so 5 s is the conservative direction for a rate budget.

worker_shapes.what: Prefix-replay teleport (Theoria.md:299's 前缀重放传送) and any scripted replay: fast-forward a known action prefix to reach a state. No model call between actions, so it runs at transport speed. This is the shape the rate limit is actually about.
One process stuck in the full retry envelope, the shape ACCESS_CHECK §6 named as the danger. Rate is set by the backoff schedule, which is imported from precheck.py rather than restated here.

scenarios.what: Theoria.md:299's arithmetic: 三臂 × 局数 × 回合. Three model tiers over the 4-game development pile to official baseline action counts.
scenarios._concurrency: BUDGET_REPORT quotes 178.7 h serial / 44.7 h four-way, i.e. the plan of record is 4 processes.

scenarios.what: Theoria.md:299's other two terms: 戳探 + 前缀重放传送. Scripted, think-free, and therefore the fastest thing this project runs.
scenarios.source: shape from probe_stickiness.py and canary.py; volume is a planning figure, not a measurement
scenarios._total_commands: one full prefix replay of the development pile's 3014 baseline actions (BUDGET_REPORT §3.1)

scenarios.what: The standing canary sweep. Included because the spend gate does not currently anticipate it (ACCESS_CHECK.md §'What S2 did not do') and a rate budget that omits the one recurring spender is the same omission in a second place.

The collision that actually happened: two sessions, four processes, cookie-less transport, retrying hard. Reconstructed to check whether the limit was ever genuinely in danger -- ACCESS_CHECK §6 asserted it was.

policy._warn_fraction: Report AMBER at half the documented limit. There is no Retry-After header and no RateLimit-* header to steer by (ACCESS_CHECK §6), so a client that reaches the limit finds out by being throttled. Half is the margin for a number nobody can observe approaching.
policy._max_concurrency_declared: The plan of record. `rate_budget.py` also reports the concurrency at which each shape would breach, which is the number an operator actually needs.
